Aims for consistent behavior instead of ad hoc crashes at different call sites.

result.summary: This PR makes CheckDiskSpace and FlatFileSeq::Open abort the process via std::abort() when they hit a rare, previously-uncaught filesystem exception (e.g. querying disk space or creating a directory fails), instead of letting an uncaught exception terminate the program less predictably. It adds logging of the underlying OS error before aborting and a new functional test (feature_io_errors.py) exercising three I/O-failure scenarios: scheduler disk-space check, blockfilterindex chunk allocation, and block file allocation. A new -test=blockfilterindex_small_chunks option is added to make the filter index allocate new file chunks more easily in tests.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core currently has inconsistent behavior when I/O operations like checking free disk space or creating directories throw unexpected exceptions: some call sites crash uncleanly with unhandled std::terminate, others silently swallow errors. Users hitting rare hardware issues (e.g. an unplugged external drive) get an unpredictable and hard-to-diagnose failure mode, and reviewers/maintainers face inconsistent error-handling patterns across the codebase.

open_concerns: Whether aborting the process (vs. attempting a best-effort clean shutdown/flush) is the right response to rare I/O exceptions in CheckDiskSpace/FlatFileSeq::Open (sedited, josibake, furszy, optout21).
Whether the fix belongs at this low-level primitive layer or should be handled by callers/thread boundaries catching exceptions (josibake, sedited).

Overlap and conflict with #35003 and #34132, which take a different, more graceful approach to I/O error handling in overlapping code paths; author argues those PRs remain incomplete and risk leaving mixed handling behavior.
resolved_concerns: Initial concern about the FlatFileSeq comment location was addressed by the author moving the fix in a later push (2026-07-10).

optout21: 'I have a weak inclination towards N.A.C.K-ing the approach... higher-level context-aware error handling is preferable against low-level context-free abort.'

uncertainties: Whether the broader I/O-error-handling effort (spanning #35003, #34132, and this PR) truly counts as a 'category-defining project' for utils, or is better read as three competing point-fixes; I leaned toward treating the blocking decision as P1-worthy given explicit cross-PR conflict and stalled progress cited by participants.

Whether reviewability should be downgraded given the depth of unresolved architectural disagreement; I treated it as Ready since no one has said 'wait' and the author remains actively engaged, per the rule that approach disputes affect Agreement, not Reviewability.
result.card: This PR makes CheckDiskSpace and FlatFileSeq::Open abort the process on rare, previously-uncaught filesystem exceptions (e.g. an external drive being unplugged), aiming for consistent error handling instead of ad hoc crashes. The problem it targets is real but very rare, and the change is heavily disputed: josibake, sedited, furszy, and optout21 argue that a low-level primitive shouldn't decide to abort and that graceful shutdown or exception propagation to a higher layer is safer, while the author (maflcko) argues that anything short of full, consistent handling across all call sites is pointless. This dispute is tied to two conflicting open PRs, #35003 and #34132, which take a more graceful approach to overlapping I/O error handling, and the author explicitly frames this as a decision the project needs to make before related work can proceed cleanly. The code itself is small, stable, and mergeable, so review of the current diff is not wasted, but the PR is stuck on an unresolved policy question rather than code quality.
